title: A halved risk can still be tiny

probes.question: A risk falls from 1 in 5,000 to 1 in 10,000. What is the absolute risk reduction?
True or false: a 50% relative risk reduction always means a large drop in your actual chance.

image.alt: A heap of white and yellow tablets and pills of many shapes.

body.claim: A risk can be cut in half while your actual chance barely changes.
body.why: Take a hypothetical drug that lowers the yearly risk of colon cancer from 1 case in 5,000 to 1 in 10,000. The relative risk reduction is 50%, but the absolute reduction is only 0.01%. Quoting only the relative figure can lead readers to exaggerate how effective a drug is, so look for both.
